claims.claim: Hayden Adams's essay (2026-08-18) claims Uniswap has settled more than $4.6 trillion in cumulative volume and DEX share of centralized spot volume grew from under 1% to over 20%.
Uniswap Labs announced the protocol surpassed $4 trillion cumulative volume on 2025-12-02, reaching each trillion-dollar mark faster than the last.

CoinGecko's DEX-spot-share series shows DEX share of spot volume rising from 6.9% (Jan 2024) to a peak of 24.5% (Jun 2025), then falling back to 13.6% (Jan 2026) — a swing, not a durable plateau above 20%.
The Block's DEX/CEX spot-volume ratio hit a record 24.14% in July 2026, up from 17% a year earlier, coinciding with falling CEX volume and the Robinhood Chain launch.

Uniswap's DEX market-share lead is volatile: it briefly ceded the top spot to PancakeSwap (19.4% vs 64.5%) in June 2025 after Binance routed retail flow via 'Binance Alpha 2.0' into PancakeSwap, before the spike fully reversed within 7 months.
Jack Bogle's 1976 Vanguard First Index Investment Trust was nicknamed 'Bogle's Folly' and raised only ~$11.3 million against a $50-150 million target.
Index funds' share of US long-term fund assets rose from roughly 9% (2000) to roughly 52-54% (2025), per ICI Fact Book data.

The active-to-passive shift was driven by a persistent, quantified fee gap (index funds ~0.11% vs active funds ~0.59% asset-weighted average fee) and ~88% of active US mutual funds underperforming their benchmark over 10 years (SPIVA) — a mechanical, EMH-consistent driver distinct from crowd sentiment reversal.

Loss-versus-rebalancing (LVR) theory (Milionis, Moallemi, Roughgarden, Zhang, 2022) formalizes AMM LP losses as an adverse-selection cost from stale on-chain prices, with required break-even trading volume scaling with the square of volatility — a structural drag with no analog for a passive index-fund holder.

A 2021 study of 17 Uniswap v3 pools (43% of v3 TVL) found LPs collectively earned $199.3M in fees but suffered $260.1M in impermanent/divergence loss — a net -$60.8M versus simply holding, with 49.5% of LPs individually net-negative.

Citadel Securities posted a record $12.2 billion in net trading revenue in 2025, a 25% increase over 2024's $9.7 billion, ending the year with $21 billion in trading capital and $6.5 billion in EBITDA.

Citadel Securities' revenue-to-capital ratio held roughly flat (2024: ~0.61x; 2025: ~0.58x) rather than expanding, and 2023 revenue fell 35% in a low-volatility period — evidence the business is cyclical/volatility-dependent rather than a static toll.

Citadel Securities executes more than 35% of total US retail equity market volume and holds ~30% of US listed options market share (self-reported); independent estimates put overall equity market-making share closer to 22%, with Jane Street and Hudson River Trading actively gaining share.

A Wharton study found execution quality under payment-for-order-flow varies entirely by broker: 75%+ of TD Ameritrade orders executed at mid-price-or-better versus only 25% of Robinhood orders, despite routing to the same wholesalers.
Curve's stETH/ETH pool depegged in June 2022 after Three Arrows Capital and Celsius withdrew a combined ~$780M same-day, pool TVL fell from $4.6B to ~$621M, and stETH traded as low as 0.9671 ETH.
UST/LUNA, designed around a correlated-pair peg mechanism, collapsed in May 2022, wiping out roughly $18B of UST and $40B of LUNA market value within days.

NVDA's rolling 30-day correlation with SPY has ranged 0.35-0.87 (average ~0.66-0.67), and NVDA's beta versus the market is reported in the 1.88-2.24 range across vendors — meaningfully above 1.0, indicating substantial idiosyncratic risk a NVDA/SPY pool would not hedge away.

Uniswap's DualPool hook (live 2026-07-22, Spark-built) parks idle pool capital in ERC-4626 yield vaults between swaps and pulls only the needed shortfall atomically into concentrated liquidity for the swap's duration — a yield-capture mechanism, not the cross-correlated-pair liquidity concentration the essay implies.

Robinhood Chain, an Arbitrum-tech-stack Ethereum L2, went live 2026-07-01; its tokenized 'Stock Tokens' are structured as 1:1-backed tokenized debt securities issued by a Jersey SPV (Robinhood Assets (Jersey) Limited), carrying no voting or shareholder rights, and are excluded from the US and US persons.

A material share of Robinhood Chain's tokenized-stock DEX volume is mechanically generated by memecoins using stock tokens as liquidity-pool collateral rather than by investors seeking equity exposure; Uniswap V3+V4 control roughly 99% of that DEX liquidity, leaving no independent venue to corroborate the figures.
Uniswap Labs reports more than $9.1 billion swapped across real-world-asset pools on the protocol, across 2.6 million transactions and 140,000+ wallets.

The broader tokenized real-world-asset market (ex-stablecoins) totals roughly $34.7B (2026), but a BeInCrypto/RWA survey found 55% of a $60B tokenized-asset universe by value shows zero weekly transfer activity, with only 62 of 1,289 surveyed assets holding 88% of total value.

DTCC — custodian of $114T in securities — is building its own tokenization/settlement platform under an SEC No-Action Letter, running production pilot trades from July 2026 with 50+ firms including BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan, targeting commercial launch in October 2026.

The SEC approved Nasdaq's tokenized-securities rule change (2026-03-18) on the condition that tokenized shares remain fungible with, share the same CUSIP/ticker as, and carry identical shareholder rights to the underlying share, with DTC (not an AMM) handling settlement.
ICE (NYSE's parent) formed a 50-50 joint venture with OKX (announced 2026-06-23) to put NYSE-listed stocks on-chain for roughly 120 million crypto traders, pending SEC/CFTC approval.

The SEC's January 2026 joint staff statement holds that federal securities laws apply to tokenized securities 'to the same extent' as traditional securities and creates no new exemption; Chair Atkins' anticipated 'innovation exemption' remains narrow, time-limited, and reportedly would exclude voting/dividend rights.

US equities have settled T+1 (one business day) since May 2024; a May 2026 DTCC-run consortium demonstration achieved atomic settlement of tokenized US Treasuries in under 5 seconds, but only as a pilot, not the production standard.

Uniswap's DAO activated a long-dormant fee switch in a December 2025 'UNIfication' vote, redirecting 1/4 to 1/6 of LP fees plus Unichain sequencer/MEV proceeds into a UNI burn ('token jar'), including a one-time retroactive burn of 100 million UNI (~$600M at vote-time prices) and a 20M UNI/year Labs budget starting January 2026.

Uniswap's total value locked fell from a ~$6.3B record (Aug 2025) to ~$3.31B (Mar 2026) and ~$3.42B (May 2026), tracking a broader DeFi-wide TVL contraction, even as combined V2/V3/V4 volume held up at $1.94B/24h (27.0% of DEX volume) by mid-June 2026.

UNI traded near $3.25 (market cap ~$2.03B) as of Adams's essay date, down roughly 42% from ~$5.60 in January 2026; the SEC closed its multi-year Uniswap Labs investigation with no enforcement action in February 2025, while Uniswap Labs separately settled with the CFTC for $175,000 in September 2024.
